To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the HCI-KDD combination is a promising approach to provide insight into high-dimensional biomedical data; (ii) graph-based mining and topological data mining may be of help for mapping high-dimensional data into low-dimensional representations; (iii) entropy-based data mining is a promising method for analysing high-dimensional data.
the HCI-KDD combination may help us to gain insight into complex data and that the three topics of graph-based mining, topology mining and entropy-based mining may contribute to this goal.

(a) Graph-based methods and topological data analysis are very promising for the analysis of complex, highdimensional data, (b) Entropy-based methods are very promising for analysing sparse, noisy and time-dependent data, and (c) The HCI-KDD approach is an excellent paradigm for the development of methods and tools that support human experts in their daily work.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of interactive knowledge discovery methods for personalized medicine, and we aim to provide the necessary tools for medical professionals to support their work.
the development of interactive methods to support medical experts in gaining insight into complex data and to discover knowledge that is relevant for their daily work.
the following question: How can we use machine learning methods to discover knowledge in order to support human intelligence in the analysis of high-dimensional, noisy and time-dependent data?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HCI and KDD have a bright future together, and the more they work together, the brighter the future becomes.
the HCI-KDD trend is very promising and that a concerted effort of both communities is necessary to achieve the goals of personalized medicine.
the HCI-KDD combination is a promising approach for personalized medicine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the HCI-KDD paradigm is an emerging trend in the area of interactive knowledge discovery and that the synergy of HCI and KDD is a promising approach to provide efficient and useful methods, algorithms, and tools to support human intelligence in the analysis of complex data.
the future of medicine is in modelling and understanding the complexity of patients.

the HCI-KDD community should not only be concerned with the design of the user interface, but also the data representation, and should not only focus on the design of the algorithm, but also the design of the interaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a synergistic combination of methods from HCI and KDD can be very helpful to discover knowledge and gain insight in high-dimensional data, and that this combination is of great relevance for personalized medicine and the grand goal of modelling patient complexity.
the combination of the HCI-KD-D approach and recent advances in computational methods may lead to novel and efficient solutions in the field of personalized medicine.

we can learn from the cognitive science of human perception, cognition, and decision making to improve the design of machine learning algorithms, and vice versa, that we can learn to design more human-centric algorithms by studying the cognitive processes of machine learning.
